pageCache.pageTitle: Headteacher's Welcome - Simon Langton Girls’ Grammar School
pageCache.text:
Headteacher's Welcome
Since its foundation in 1881, Langton Girls’ has provided students with a challenging academic curriculum, outstanding pastoral care and a wider educational experience that develops the whole person beyond the confines of the taught curriculum. These three principles continue as our foundations to this day; we take pride in the work we do to support and guide ambitious, confident, independent and creative young women, preparing them for their lives to come.
Being a part of the Langton Family is not just about support, it is also about challenge. It is about working hard and recognising that through application and commitment we fulfil our potential. It is about the value of competition and making progress by learning from our failures, be them personal, scientific, creative or sporting, and using this learning to achieve future success.
The Langton Family also represents diversity; as a community we recognise and celebrate our differences, and through this develop deeper understanding and appreciation, becoming collectively closer and stronger.
We not only provide outstanding, modern, facilities, but an educationally rich and safe environment, one that encourages our students to make the most of the Langton Extended Curriculum, to challenge themselves outside of their classrooms, and to grow as individuals. We support them in pursuing different pathways, preparing them for the university places and careers to come, providing a base from which to build happy lives.
Please take some time to browse our website and find out more about us. We are proud of our school and what we do, I hope it is clear why.
And if you should have any questions, please don’t hesitate to get in touch.
Paper copies of information held on the school website can be requested from the School Office.

pageCache.pageTitle: National Theatre Classics and Drama Trip Report - News - Simon Langton Girls’ Grammar School
pageCache.text:
National Theatre Classics and Drama Trip Report
On 15th October 2025, our Classics and Drama Year 13 students had the opportunity to see the National Theatre’s production of The Bacchae at the Olivier Theatre — a bold, modern interpretation of Euripides’ Greek tragedy, directed by Indhu Rubasingham.
The performance explored themes of power, identity, and rebellion through stunning visual design. One moment that stood out to the students was when King Pentheus opened a wardrobe glowing with golden light — a striking symbol of transformation and the power. Later, shimmering mirror balls cast golden reflections across the theatre, creating a lively, immersive atmosphere that captivated the audience.
Students were particularly impressed by how lighting and projections were used to enhance the drama and connect this ancient story to modern audiences. The production was praised by the students for its creativity, symbolism, and the way it reimagined a timeless tale for today’s world. It was a lovely way to end Term 1 with a cross curricular visit to the National Theatre.

pageCache.text:
SEND and The Learning Base
Our SENDCO is Mrs Charman and our Deputy SENDCO is Mrs Wisden. To contact Mrs Charman, Mrs Wisden or The Learning Base team please use either of the following contact email addresses:
SEND@langton.kent.sch.uk for SEND enquiries. This will reach our SENDCO Mrs Annika Charman and SENDCO Deputy Mrs Chloe Wisden.
thelearningbase@langton.kent.sch.uk for day-to-day updates or questions, this will reach our LSA team.
SEND Local Offer - please click HERE for information
'Information Advice and Support Kent' (IASK) can be found HERE.
They provide a special educational needs and disabilities information, advice and support service for parents/carers of a child or young person with special educational needs or a disability, and children or young people up to the age of 25 with special educational needs or disability.
FACE - please click HERE
FACE gives practical, accessible and affordable support to parents (as well as schools and organisations). Parents can access relevant advice, up to date information and easy to apply interventions, delivered via online and in-person talks, group sessions, videos and one-to-one support on a wide range of topics, including SEND.
SEND Mainstream Core Standards
Mainstream Core Standards
Simon Langton Girls' Grammar School aims to meet the special educational needs of all our students as defined in the SEND policy which can be found within the policies area.
The school provides for students who can access mainstream education and who may have SEND that is categorised as follows:
Cognitive and Learning Needs
• Specific Learning Difficulties (SpLd)
• Moderate Learning Difficulties (MLD)
Communication and Interactive Needs
• Speech, Language and Communication Needs (SLCN)
• Autistic Spectrum Condition (ASC)
Social, Emotional and Mental Health Needs (SEMH)
Sensory and/or Physical Needs
• Hearing Impairment (HI)
• Visual Impairment (VI)
Weekly SEND briefings with LSAs have ensured the department's vision is being developed and shared. There has been a focus on training for LSAs with sessions on Dyspraxia, Sensory Preferences, Social Stories, Dyslexia, Exam Training, strategies to support students with ASC; strategies to support students with Speech and Language needs. Training sessions by the SENDCO have been delivered to new staff.
The SENDCO meets with the Key Stage 3,4 and 5 teams, senior management team, pastoral managers and academic leads every term to discuss identified students within the year groups and the interventions put in place. A rolling record is kept of the strategies offered.

Careers Advice & Guidance
Our University and Career Education Lead is Sophie Cavey.
Contact information: Telephone: 01227 463711. Email: scavey@langton.kent.sch.uk
All students are entitled to careers education, information, advice, and guidance as part of their Langton Journey and our careers programme has been developed in alignment with our Langton Values. We are committed to ensuring that our students acquire the necessary values, skills, and knowledge to appropriately develop and manage their careers learning and aspirations. Our careers programme ensures that all students are able to make informed, independent, and ambitious decisions at each key transition point. They leave us equipped with the confidence and skills needed to help them navigate their chosen pathway and the world of work. Students receive a comprehensive programme of careers education delivered through tutorials, workshops, assemblies, Personal Development lessons, enrichment, curriculum alignment, and stand-alone events.The programme is updated annually.

Saxons Elite Cheer
Saxons Elite is an Allstar Cheerleading team based in Canterbury, Kent, and has been running since 2008, where it began as 'Saxon Stars'.
We are a fully inclusive team and have classes for ages 3+ and all abilities. Our Allstar and Prep athletes compete throughout the year around the country and internationally. Our teams have always been and continue to be successful at various competitions and event providers, and we have been awarded both National and European titles.
We aim to inspire young people in our community to be part of a team, learn new skills, make friends for life and promote a healthy lifestyle.
All of our amazing Coaching Team are qualified and are or have been competitive cheerleaders, competing at World's and Summit level. They are first aid trained and Enhanced DBS checked. They all have a wealth of experience and knowledge in both Cheer and Tumble.
We always welcome new team members to join the Saxons family.
For more information please visit our website HERE
1st Sturry Explorer Scouts
We are a group for young people aged 13½ to 18, and we are currently welcoming new members.
We meet weekly and offer a range of fun and exciting activities that help young people build confidence, teamwork, leadership skills, and friendships. Activities include camping, hiking, outdoor adventures, games, community projects, and much more throughout the year.
The cost to attend is £4 per night, and we aim to make the group welcoming and accessible to everyone.
If you would like further information, please feel free to contact us sturry-explorers@hotmail.com

Law Pathway: Irwin Mitchell Careers Talk
Just before half term, we were delighted to welcome school alumna Clare Wiseman, Head of Family Law at Irwin Mitchell, to speak to students as part of our Law Pathway programme. With over 30 years’ experience and an international reputation in family law, Clare shared fascinating insights into her route into the profession and spoke in depth about her experiences within family law. Clare also offered valuable advice on what makes a strong applicant to competitive firms, highlighting the importance of commercial awareness, resilience, initiative and excellent communication skills. Students gained insight into how the legal landscape is evolving, and practical steps they can take now to strengthen future applications. It was an inspiring and informative session that gave students a real understanding of life in the legal profession, and we are very grateful to Clare for her time and expertise. Dr Cavey

Young Carers
Imago Young Carers is a social action charity working across Kent, Medway, East Sussex and London
In 2024 we celebrated 60 years of supporting people and communities across the South East. We are proud that our services support thousands of people to make positive changes and improve their lives.
We are a resilient and diverse organisation, focused on providing high quality services with consistency and care. With strong leadership and a dedicated, and skilled staff team, we are committed to creating opportunities and delivering the best support possible for some of the most vulnerable in our communities.
Helping young people to thrive.
We provide emotional and practical support for young carers, helping them to balance their caring responsibilities with being children.
We also offer services that support disabled children and their families, helping them to gain independence, learn new skills and have fun in a supportive space with others.
Young carers
Being a young carer can mean different things to different people. If you are under 18 and providing care, it's important to know that support is available. Find out how we can help. Click HERE
Young Carer Champions
We have three members of our pastoral team who are 'Young Carer Champions'. Mrs Booth, Mrs Bramwell and Mrs Liston. Please contact the school if you would like to talk to either of them regarding young carers.
Support in school
For young carer students, we run a weekly support club which is held every Wednesday, in the conference room. For period 4 lunch, 12:45-1:15pm this is with Mrs Liston and for period 5 lunch, 1:45-2:15pm this is with Mrs Booth.
We have also successfully ran two young carers trips which have been free of charge for the students due to the generous funding from the Langton Family Association (LFA).
We work very closely with Imago, the external young carers support team and they will come into school to speak with young carers, either in a group or 1:1 setting. Our allocated worker from Imago is Tina Culver.
